iut_type: End Product (Ricoh Imaging camera prototype), UFP-only (sink-only) certification feasibility with sub-threshold Source current and DisplayPort Alt Mode
customer_question: Our camera prototype's Source output current is only about 200mA, below the 500mA/900mA thresholds that disqualify it from DRP (dual-role power) certification. Given that, can we still obtain UFP-only (sink-only) certification? Also, if our Source current falls short, what can we trim from the quoted test scope to reduce cost while still getting DRP evaluation testing done?
question_variants: If we give up on PD logo certification due to insufficient Source current, what costs can be reduced from the quote?
Can a product default to UFP mode (with user-switchable DFP) still be certified as UFP-only without testing the DFP mode?
Is UFP-only certification possible at all if the product needs to support DisplayPort Source functionality?
actual_issue: The customer's camera prototype had a Source output current (~200mA) well below the DRP eligibility threshold, and they wanted to know both (a) what cost reductions were available if abandoning DRP/PD certification, and (b) whether UFP-only (sink-only) certification was achievable given the product's need to support DisplayPort Source functionality, which has its own power-role requirements that conflict with a sink-only declaration.
plain_english_explanation: If the customer commits to DRP evaluation testing regardless, no cost reduction was offered — DRP testing was treated as a fixed requirement in the quoted scope once requested. Separately, on the UFP-only feasibility question: per the 'DisplayPort Alt Mode on USB Type-C Standard,' a DisplayPort Source role requires either the Power Role to be Source, or a DRP that performs DFP-initiated Discovery/Entry — meaning a strictly UFP-only (sink-only) declared device cannot support DP Source functionality at all. This created a direct conflict between the customer's product specification (needing DP Source capability) and a UFP-only certification path, since UFP-only fundamentally cannot satisfy the DP Source role requirements. The customer was advised to consult their IC vendor about this specification conflict before deciding on a certification path. A defaulting-to-one-mode design (e.g., defaults to UFP but is user-switchable to DFP) does not exempt the non-default mode from testing — both modes must still be tested and pass for full dual-role logo certification, regardless of which mode is the factory default.
consultant_answer: Regarding cost: since you're committing to DRP evaluation testing either way, no reduction applies for that scope. On the UFP-only question: per the DisplayPort Alt Mode on USB Type-C Standard, a DP Source role requires either a Source Power Role or a DRP capable of DFP-initiated Discovery/Entry — so a strictly UFP-only (sink-only) device cannot support DP Source at all. Since your product needs DP Source functionality, this is a direct conflict with a UFP-only certification path; we'd recommend consulting your IC vendor about resolving this specification conflict. Also note that a product defaulting to one mode but user-switchable to the other still requires both modes to be tested and pass — the default-mode framing doesn't exempt the non-default mode.
decision_logic: DisplayPort Source role support has its own power-role prerequisite (Source or DFP-initiated DRP) independent of USB-PD certification tier; a UFP-only (sink-only) declared device is structurally incompatible with DP Source functionality, so any product needing DP Source must pursue DRP or DFP certification regardless of its actual measured Source current, and a sub-threshold Source current that disqualifies DRP eligibility creates a genuine specification conflict requiring IC-vendor-level resolution rather than a certification-path workaround.
final_recommendation: Before quoting or scoping a UFP-only certification path, confirm whether the product needs DisplayPort Source functionality — if so, flag the DP Alt Mode power-role prerequisite immediately, since it forecloses UFP-only as an option, and direct the customer to resolve the underlying power-current shortfall with their IC vendor rather than treating it as a certification-process question.
risk_if_done_wrong: Proceeding toward a UFP-only certification path for a product that also needs DisplayPort Source functionality would result in a fundamental, unresolvable conflict discovered only at testing time, since UFP-only literally cannot satisfy the DP Source role's power-role prerequisite, wasting the cost and time already spent pursuing that path.
